newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' SEC sees new insider trading rule.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' SEC sees new insider trading rule.

text.p: The Philippines' Securities and Exhange Commission (SEC) said on Thursday a stricter insider trading rule is expected to be enforced within the next few weeks.
SEC chairman Perfecto Yasay said in a news conference that Congress was set to approve the Securities Regulations and Enforcement Act of 1997 "within the next few weeks or so."

Under the new rule, the burden of proof will shift from the SEC to the company director, official or employee accused of trading their own shares on material information which has not been disclosed to the public.
"The burden of proof shifts from the SEC to the company officer ... He must show proof that, in fact, the information is public in nature or there is no such information," Yasay said.
Yasay also said family members of company employees or directors can also be charged with insider trading. Violators are liable to a jail term of 20 years and fines of 500,000 pesos each.
Nobody has been tried so far for insider trading in the Philippines.
The new law would also give the SEC the power to vest a stock exchange with self-regulatory organisation (SRO) status.
The SEC is expected to grant SRO status to the Philippine Exchange (PSE) once the bourse complies with all the conditions set by the regulator which include an improved listing rule.
"As I gathered from the leadership of the stock exchange, they're giving themselves anywhere between now and October to be able to comply with all of these conditions," Yasay said.
